steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Ensemble performance assesses your ability to LISTEN and RESPOND to other musicians — not just play your part accurately. | Key Fact: Balance means adjusting your volume so each part is heard appropriately; tuning means matching pitch with others continuously. | Key Fact: Following a leader (conductor or lead player) requires watching for cues, tempo changes and dynamic adjustments in real time. | Key Fact: Chamber music (string quartet, wind quintet) demands the highest level of ensemble skill — every player must lead and follow simultaneously.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how ensemble performance are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use ensemble performance. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use ensemble performance in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
